newsitem.title: GERMANY: Air Lanka increases Colombo-FRA flights.
newsitem.headline: Air Lanka increases Colombo-FRA flights.

text.p: Air Lanka said it will add a fourth weekly Colombo-Frankfurt flight from December 15.
The airline's Germany cargo sales executive, Hiran Houx, said the extra flight would increase weekly ex-Germany cargo capacity by up to 40 percent depending on passenger loads.
He told Reuters in an interview: "We will have an additional weekly flight either on Thursdays or Saturdays with a Tristar L1011-500."
The airline flies currently thrice-weekly between Colombo and Frankfurt with an Airbus A340-300 and also has weekly departures from Zurich and Amsterdam.
Houx said Air Lanka was carrying 17-22 tonnes of freight per flight and had an ex-Germany load factor of approaching 100 percent at present.
"This is about 10-12 percent growth in tonnage. Last year we had a load factor of 90-95 percent," he told Reuters in an interview.
The airline forecast an ex-Germany tonnage of 2,200 tonnes for 1996, he added.
More than half of the cargo was destined for Colombo, and the rest went on to Bangkok, Hong Kong, Singapore and Tokyo, he said.

Air Lanka also had fixed allotments on the weekly flights from Amsterdam and Zurich for Germany, which was the second-largest European market after Britain, he added. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
